correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the general proof. With the first three vertices infinity, 0, 1, the first two cross-intersections are [1:0:de] and [1+e+f:ef:ef]; they give the stated quadratic on the conic. The tangent condition excludes precisely the q-2 distinct inverse pairs. For a proposed finite root t other than 0 or 1, N=td(1+e) is nonzero, so the four forbidden denominators/values for f=N/P are disjoint. P=N gives t=de and dP=N gives t=d,e. P=0 and eP=N each exclude two sets of size q-2 and a disjoint set parametrized by nonzero k other than 1 and the roots of k^2+k+1. This gives the two stated subfield corrections. An exterior pair comprises conjugate nonrational parameters; the affine subgroup is already transitive on those individual parameters, and the conic group is transitive on rational points and rational pairs. The sharp triple normalization, free 12-element dihedral action, and the three line class sizes give the asserted per-line counts. The secant factor is positive even with the maximum correction 4 for q>=8; all other factors are positive, and q=2,4 have too few vertices. Independent exact replay: python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_nov24_pascal.py, using different binary field presentations and counting normalized triples by the absolute trace of de/B^2 (or B=0 for tangency), not by the dossier's point-incidence exclusions. This matched all three multiplicities at q=8,16,32,64,128, including (112,21,117) and (3360,1920,3536). The finite replay corroborates the symbolic proof; it is not an all-fields verification on its own. The frozen script was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: A natural finite-geometry incidence invariant is fully determined in an exceptional characteristic where all tangents are concurrent and quadratic splitting works differently. The theorem gives the first possible binary field for all-line coverage and distinguishes fibers across every extension by a precise order-three subfield correction; it is more than a six-set experiment or a re-normalized complex count.
